translations.literal: " Bochao brandished his blade and glanced at Que, saying, "I know you—but does my blade know you?
translations.idiomatic: " Bochao drew his blade and looked at Que. "I know you," he said, "but does my blade?

sentences.zh: 」確於是流涕而出，遂入城。

translations.literal: " Que thereupon wept as he went out and then entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: " Que wept as he left, then entered the city.

sentences.zh: 及景背盟復圍城，城陷，確排闥入，啓高祖曰：「城已陷矣。

translations.literal: When Jing broke the truce and again besieged the city, the city fell. Que pushed open the inner gate and reported to Gaozu, "The city has fallen.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing broke the truce and besieged the city again, the walls fell. Que burst through the inner gate and told Emperor Wu, "The city is lost.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「猶可一戰不？

translations.literal: " Gaozu said, "Can we still fight one battle?
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wu asked, "Can we still fight one more battle?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「不可。

translations.literal: " He answered, "We cannot.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "No.

sentences.zh: 臣向者親格戰，勢不能禁，自縋下城，僅得至此。

translations.literal: Your subject just now fought hand to hand and could not hold them back. I lowered myself by rope from the wall and barely reached here.
translations.idiomatic: I was fighting hand to hand and could not hold them. I let myself down from the wall on a rope and barely made it here.

sentences.zh: 」高祖歎曰：「自我得之，自我失之，亦復何恨。

translations.literal: " Gaozu sighed and said, "I gained it myself and I lose it myself—what regret is there?
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wu sighed and said, "I won it myself and I lose it myself—what is there to regret?

sentences.zh: 」乃使確爲慰勞文。

translations.literal: " He then had Que draft a letter of consolation.
translations.idiomatic: " He then had Que draft a letter of consolation to the troops.

sentences.zh: 確旣出見景，景愛其膂力，恒令在左右。

translations.literal: When Que went out and saw Jing, Jing admired his physical strength and always kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Que went out to see Hou Jing, Hou Jing admired his strength and always kept him close.

sentences.zh: 後從景行，見天上飛鳶，羣虜爭射不中，確射之，應弦而落。

translations.literal: Later, following Jing on the march, they saw a kite flying in the sky. The bandits all shot at it but missed. Que shot it, and it fell at the twang of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Later, marching with Hou Jing, they saw a kite overhead. The rebels all shot and missed. Que shot once and brought it down.

sentences.zh: 賊徒忿嫉，咸勸除之。

translations.literal: The bandits were resentful and jealous, and all urged that he be eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were jealous and urged that he be killed.

sentences.zh: 先是攜王遣人密導確，確謂使者曰：「侯景輕佻，可一夫力致，確不惜死，正欲手刃之；

translations.literal: Earlier Prince Yo had sent someone in secret to guide Que. Que told the envoy, "Hou Jing is frivolous and can be brought down by one man's strength. I do not spare my life and mean to kill him with my own hand;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Prince Yo had sent a secret envoy to Que. Que told him, "Hou Jing is reckless and could be brought down by one man. I do not fear death—I mean to kill him with my own hand;

sentences.zh: 但未得其便耳。

translations.literal: only I have not yet found the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: I only lack the chance.

sentences.zh: 卿還啓家王，願勿以爲念也。

translations.literal: When you return, report to my prince and ask that he not worry on my account.
translations.idiomatic: Go back and tell my father not to worry about me.

sentences.zh: 」事未遂而爲賊所害。

translations.literal: " The affair did not succeed, and he was killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he could act, the rebels killed him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自周、漢廣樹籓屏，固本深根；

translations.literal: The historian says: From Zhou and Han, feudal screens were widely planted to strengthen the root deep in the soil;
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: From Zhou and Han onward, feudal princes were widely enfeoffed to secure the dynasty at its roots;

sentences.zh: 高祖之封建，將遵古制也。

translations.literal: Gaozu's enfeoffments were intended to follow the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's enfeoffments were meant to follow that ancient model.

sentences.zh: 南康、廬陵並以宗室之貴，據磐石之重，績以孝著，續以勇聞。

translations.literal: Nankang and Luling both, by the honor of the imperial clan, held the weight of bedrock. Ji was noted for filial piety, Xu for courage.
translations.idiomatic: Nankang and Luling, as members of the imperial house, held the weight of bedrock posts. Ji was known for filial piety, Xu for courage.

sentences.zh: 綸聰警有才學，性險躁，屢以罪黜，及太清之亂，忠孝獨存，斯可嘉矣。

translations.literal: Lun was clever and alert, with talent and learning, but his nature was dangerous and restless. Repeatedly he was dismissed for offenses. Yet in the chaos of Taiqing, loyalty and filial piety alone remained in him—this is worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was clever and learned, but rash and volatile; he was repeatedly punished for offenses. Yet amid the Taiqing turmoil he alone kept faith and filial duty—this is praiseworthy.
